auxiliary_scientific_checks.claim: The finite-presentation reduction and the finite-generation transfer
auxiliary_scientific_checks.check: The finite-presentation assumption is introduced only after replacing the original finitely generated domain by a finitely presented cover with the same limit group. It is therefore available to the approximation construction in Section 9. In the proof of Theorem 2.8, the finite shortening chain maps each stably parabolic subgroup injectively into a stably parabolic subgroup of the terminal group. The latter is finitely generated by Theorem 4.19. The transfer to a subgroup uses abelianity (Lemma 4.6), since arbitrary subgroups of finitely generated groups need not be finitely generated. Edge groups are covered by the preceding stably parabolic assertions. This verifies the logical implication, conditional on the hypotheses and the invoked results.
auxiliary_scientific_checks.limits: The full proofs of Lemma 4.6 and all geometric inputs to Theorem 4.19 were not recursively rederived. Page 15 was read as extracted text by this auxiliary; its source-image inspection belongs to the root's separate evidence.

auxiliary_scientific_checks.claim: The Section 6 route to finite generation
auxiliary_scientific_checks.check: The relevant splitting is finite and edge-twisted: the two peripheral kernels at an abelian valence-two vertex have trivial intersection, and the edge quotients are finitely generated. Theorem 6.7 then gives finite generation of the type-B vertex groups; Corollary 3.18 and Corollary 6.4 supply the subsequent transfer to the original stably parabolic group. Lemma 6.13 expressly states free abelian of rank at most 2 for the indicated quotient. Thus an objection based only on the distinction between finite rank and finite generation would misread this statement.
auxiliary_scientific_checks.limits: The collapsed-space and cut-point geometry behind Proposition 6.3 and Lemma 6.13, including Proposition 5.1, Lemma 5.5 and Proposition 5.17, was not fully independently checked. The result of Corollary 3.18 and the peripheral-intersection result used in Proposition 6.6 remain declared dependencies.

auxiliary_scientific_checks.claim: Lifting squared Nielsen moves in the virtually abelian case
auxiliary_scientific_checks.check: For the central extension considered in Lemma 8.13, let c_x=t^{-1}xtx be central for x in the abelian index-at-most-two subgroup. The proposed lift of the squared Nielsen move sends g to g h^2 c_h^{-1}, fixes t and the other indicated basis elements, and preserves the conjugation relation because c_{g h^2 c_h^{-1}}=c_g. This follows from multiplicativity of x to c_x on the abelian subgroup and c_z=z^2 for central z. The inverse basis move exists. The incident edge subgroup intersected with the abelian subgroup lies in the fixed peripheral subgroup; the reflected coset calculation gives conjugation by h^{-n} for the appropriate exponent n. These checks support the claimed edge compatibility. The QH-type lifting used later also requires Lemma 8.14, not only the virtually abelian calculation in Lemma 8.13.
auxiliary_scientific_checks.limits: The existence and full structure of the modular splitting in Theorem 8.12, its cited external inputs, and the complete QH lifting argument were not recursively reproved.

auxiliary_scientific_checks.claim: Approximation, kernel containment and preservation of parabolic groups
auxiliary_scientific_checks.check: The approximation uses finite graphs of groups and factorizations phi_i=lambda_i xi_i. Replacing lambda_i by its short representative defines eta_i=hat(lambda_i) xi_i. Consequently every element killed in an approximating quotient remains killed by the shortened sequence, giving Ker^omega(phi_i) contained in Ker^omega(eta_i) and the induced quotient of limit groups. The finite graph and finite edge paths used for Lemma 9.8 provide a uniform bound on the Bass-Serre displacement after the indicated conjugations. Lemma 9.9 uses conjugation on stably parabolic subgroups, so their nontrivial elements remain nontrivial in the shortening quotient. This is the preservation needed by the later finite-generation transfer. When the shortening quotient is an isomorphism, Lemma 9.10 permits the existing geometric decomposition to be used on the quotient.
auxiliary_scientific_checks.limits: This checks the stated containment and preservation mechanism. It does not replace the whole construction of compatible relative JSJ decompositions or independently prove every result cited from [19] or Appendix B.

auxiliary_scientific_checks.check: The two-generator procedure subtracts even multiples of one translation from the other. For an irrational ratio this process cannot terminate at an exact rational equality; successive suitable steps reduce a larger absolute translation, and the ratio-at-least-one-half phase decreases by a fixed positive gap until a halving step becomes possible. Interchanging the roles and repeating makes both selected translation lengths arbitrarily small. For higher rank, density supplies an irrational pair; after shortening that pair, each remaining generator can be reduced by even multiples of a small selected generator. This supplies the reduction implicit in the text's two-generator simplification. No numerical experiment or author code was used.
auxiliary_scientific_checks.limits: This is a direct algebraic check of the stated line-action mechanism, not a full reconstruction of the Rips-machine decomposition used by Theorem 9.12.

auxiliary_scientific_checks.claim: The noncircular descending-chain argument and the finite resolution
locators: Theorem 4.20 as restated and proved on pp. 47-48
auxiliary_scientific_checks.check: The finite-ball maximal-kernel choices first construct a particular diagonal limit R_infinity. A proper infinite chain starting at that R_infinity would kill an element of some finite ball that survives R_infinity; composing with R_n produces a larger kernel on that ball than the maximally chosen next quotient, a contradiction. This establishes descending-chain termination for this particular R_infinity before global termination is proved. It then permits finitely many T-shortening steps followed by finitely many C-shortening steps. Lemmas 9.8-9.10 and Theorem 9.12 supply the required preservation and terminal nondivergence; Theorem 4.19 gives finite generation of terminal parabolics; Theorem 2.7 gives factoring at the non-T-divergent stage. The cited [17] arguments transfer factoring back through the T-shortening sequence. Factoring contradicts the diagonal choice of a witness killed at the next limit stage but not by the chosen psi_n. Only after this argument does Theorem 4.20 use global descending-chain termination to build its finite C-shortening resolution. There is no circular invocation of Theorem 4.20 in the construction of the special diagonal limit.
auxiliary_scientific_checks.local_notation: The final kernel-containment display on p. 47 is reversed as printed. The actual implication needed is Ker(phi_infinity^(n+1)) contained in Ker(psi_infinity) contained in Ker(psi_n), with the second containment supplied by factoring. The selected witness lies in the first kernel and outside Ker(psi_n). Correcting this direction gives the stated contradiction without changing the mathematical strategy.
auxiliary_scientific_checks.limits: The cited external factoring-transfer lemmas from [17] and the complete Theorem 9.12 shortening proof remain dependencies. The reversed printed containment is a local notation correction, not an established new failure of the main theorem.

auxiliary_scientific_checks.claim: The algebra in Appendix A and its exact boundary
auxiliary_scientific_checks.check: For A.1, the elements of the finitely generated abelian N whose K-coset meets L form a subgroup N_0. The condition K intersect L={1} gives a unique correcting element of K and a surjection from N_0 onto <N,K> intersect L. For A.2, amalgam normal-form reductions replace K syllables from <S_2> by words in S_3; when G is finitely generated, S_2 is finite and its intersection with K is finitely generated because <S_2> is finitely generated abelian. For A.3, adjoining the two finite intersection generating sets produces a finitely generated N_1 satisfying the two saturation inclusions with K and L. The subgroup M' generated in equation (6) is finitely generated. The larger N_2 in equation (7) need not be finitely generated; the proof uses it only to obtain the two intersection identities. These identities close the Britton reductions and show M=M'. The final induction for Theorem 6.7 collapses all edges not incident to one chosen type-A vertex. The resulting one-type-A graph is covered by A.3 or A.4; the collapsed type-B groups are then finitely generated and the induction applies to their smaller edge-twisted subgraphs.
auxiliary_scientific_checks.limits: Lemma A.4's proof is explicitly omitted by the source. This auxiliary did not independently supply that omitted proof. Theorem 6.7's induction was checked conditional on A.4 as well as A.3; the record does not claim a complete new proof of the whole appendix.
